I am an old man, 66 now, been working this land 50 years. My wife and me, just the two of us on 14.5 mu. Let me think how I do this year, same as most years.

Wheat first. I plant in October after the maize comes off. I buy two bags of compound fertilizer for each mu — that's what the dealer in town sells, the 15-15-15 kind, about 50 jin each bag... no wait, one bag is 40 kg. So two bags make 80 kg of compound per mu, mixed into the soil when I plow. Then in spring when the wheat turns green again, I spread one bag of urea per mu, maybe 40 kg. My neighbor Old Wang did this for years and gets good wheat, so I do the same. If I put less I worry the wheat goes yellow and thin.

Water — I pump from the well. Once before winter so the ground freezes wet, once when it greens up in spring, once when the stalks stand up, once when the ears fill. Four times. If rain comes good maybe three. For spray, once for the weeds in spring, once for the bugs and the head disease near harvest. Two sprays.

I use the rotary machine — everyone uses it now, cheaper than plowing deep. The tractor man charges by the mu. I buy the wheat seed from the agri-store, they tell me which is good this year, I take what my neighbors took. Improved kind.

Maize I plant right after wheat harvest in June, no time to plow, I just drill seed into the stubble. No-tillage they call it, but I just call it "planting into the stubble." I use hybrid seed for maize, everyone does, the old kind gives nothing. One bag compound per mu at planting, then one bag urea per mu when the plant is knee-high, maybe 40 kg. That's how my son-in-law does it on his land too.

Water for maize — if summer rains come I don't pump. Usually I pump two times, once after planting if dry, once when it tassels. Spray twice, once for weeds when small, once for the borer worm.

Yield — good year wheat gives me about 500 kg per mu, maize about 600 kg. Bad year less. I count on this.
